Class Mui2UI

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.integration.mui2.Mui2UI
All Implemented Interfaces:
HostUI
Direct Known Subclasses:
SyncedMui2UI
public class Mui2UI extends Object implements HostUI
Adapts a ModularUI screen and its Minecraft wrapper to a desktop window.

If no wrapper exists, construction makes a client-only ModularContainer and wrapper. A server-bound screen must instead retain its existing wrapper and use a synchronized session. Minecraft and ModularUI global screen state are both borrowed through scopes before drawing, ticking, or delivering widget input. The historical MUI2 name is retained while this port targets ModularUI 3.

    • scope

      public Scope scope()
      Returns the retained scope that enters Minecraft's screen state before ModularUI's state.

      Supplies the temporary Minecraft/framework state needed by this screen. A scope borrows shared state on entry and returns it on restoration. HostUI's default implementation returns a scope that changes no state.

      For example, ScreenScope temporarily sets Minecraft's current screen to the hosted GUI. Return a retained scope instance: the host calls this method separately for entry and restoration. Creating a new scope on each call would lose the saved state. The host enters and restores it around layout, updates, input, and drawing; do not enter it again inside those callbacks.

      Specified by:
      scope in interface HostUI
      Returns:
      non-null scope retained for entry and restoration

    • update

      public void update()
      Ticks the ModularUI context, then calls the screen's update hook.

      Advances the visible screen's logic on a client tick. HostUI's default implementation does nothing.

      Ticking is independent of the window's frame-rate limit. First layout happens during rendering, so this callback can run before onResize. Initialize any state needed here before opening the window, or wait until layout has supplied the required dimensions.

      Specified by:
      update in interface HostUI

    • dispose

      public void dispose()
      Closes an open ModularUI panel manager, then disposes it once closed. An already-disposed manager is ignored.

      Releases resources owned by this adapter when its hosted entry is removed. Do not dispose borrowed global Minecraft or framework resources. The hosted entry prevents duplicate disposal calls for that entry.

      Disposal does not enter this adapter's scope. Do not assume that temporary Minecraft state supplied by the scope is active during cleanup.

      Specified by:
      dispose in interface HostUI

    • clearComponentFocus

      public void clearComponentFocus()
      Clears the ModularUI widget context's focused component.

      Clears focused-widget state owned by this adapter. HostUI's default implementation does nothing.

      The HEI wrapper calls this when it consumes a mouse press. Implementations clear their own widget focus without changing which native desktop window has focus.

      Specified by:
      clearComponentFocus in interface HostUI

    • onResize

      public void onResize(int width, int height)
      Passes the initialized GUI dimensions to ModularUI for relayout.

      Responds after Minecraft has initialized the screen at its current GUI size.

      The host calls this during first layout, when the scaled dimensions change, or after an explicit relayout request. Returning to a parent screen can call it again with the same dimensions.

      Drawing and pointer callbacks use these same GUI units. For example, a 480 by 320 GUI has its center at (240, 160), even if its framebuffer is larger. Use these dimensions for layout and hit testing without applying the display scale again.

      Specified by:
      onResize in interface HostUI
      Parameters:
      width - scaled GUI width, not native drawable pixel width
      height - scaled GUI height, not native drawable pixel height

    • onMouseDrag

      public void onMouseDrag(int mouseX, int mouseY, int button, long heldMs)
      Sets the context's drag button and calls ModularUI's drag handler. Pointer coordinates come from the preceding hover update.

      Continues a drag while the adapter's remembered button remains held.

      The default dispatcher calls this on each input pass while a drag is active, even when the pointer has not moved. Timing starts when it handles the press, so time spent waiting in the native event queue is not included.

      Specified by:
      onMouseDrag in interface HostUI
      Parameters:
      mouseX - current pointer X in GUI units
      mouseY - current pointer Y in GUI units from the top
      button - button that started the drag
      heldMs - elapsed wall-clock milliseconds since the dispatcher handled the press

    • onKeyTyped

      public void onKeyTyped(char typedChar, int keyCode)
      Offers key presses to ModularUI widgets before handling Escape or the inventory key. If widgets do not consume either key, it cancels an active drag or closes the top framework panel.

      Handles a legacy key-down event; text composition uses HostUI.onTextInput(String).

      In the default dispatcher, even a letter-key press normally carries a zero character. Use the key code for shortcuts and navigation, and handle decoded text in onTextInput rather than deriving it from that code.

      Specified by:
      onKeyTyped in interface HostUI
      Parameters:
      typedChar - legacy character; normally zero for physical key transitions
      keyCode - LWJGL2-compatible key code
